item.text:
## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp semantics and NULL documentation should be corrected because they give consumers incorrect lifecycle information.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the current-state process model and documents its timestamp and NULL semantics.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Exclude start timestamps from finished_at — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, the new column reports `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z` as its finish time. The CASE selects start events, while `models/schema.yml:11` defines the column as the time the process finished. — Consumers can treat running processes as completed and calculate completion metrics from the wrong lifecycle event.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Describe NULL in terms of the latest event — For process 30, “NULL means the process has never been started” is false: its `started` event precedes `cleared`. The SQL expression `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` examines only the latest event. — After a started process is cleared, consumers following this documentation incorrectly classify it as never started.

(none)
